obligations.behavior: --dry-run changes no file and lists exactly the files a real pass then changes; results on stdout, errors on stderr, exit 0/1/2; the bare noun prints the overview; explain resolves records, records overview and records prune
obligations.source_text: a 'records' CLI noun: 'records prune [--dry-run] [--keep-days N] [--json]' compresses and deletes exactly as the daemon would and prints what it did / would do, plus 'records overview' (rubric overview_cli_noun_exists) and explain-catalog entries

obligations.seam: _file_logger in cli/_commands/governing.py (tests with a tiny cap on tmp_path)
obligations.behavior: the log never exceeds the cap plus one line; on rotation the old contents land in governor.log.1.gz (one generation, replaced on the next rotation) and the next line starts a fresh governor.log
obligations.source_text: governor.log rotates when it exceeds a cap (proposed log_max_mib = 10 in [daemon]): the current file becomes governor.log.1.gz, one rotated generation kept; _file_logger (cli/_commands/governing.py:231-239) stays append-and-close per line

obligations.behavior: a crash injected between write, fsync and rename leaves the raw day or a complete .gz plus at most one .tmp; a later pass removes only a .tmp older than 1 hour; files not named YYYYMMDD.jsonl(.gz) are never removed
obligations.source_text: retention only touches files named YYYYMMDD.jsonl / YYYYMMDD.jsonl.gz in <data_dir>/records and governor.log(.1.gz); any other file in the data dir is never deleted; compression writes to a temp file and renames, so a crash leaves either the raw day or the finished .gz, never a torn one

obligations.seam: Daemon retention thread + retention.compress_day streaming (tests/test_daemon*.py, tests/test_retention.py)
obligations.behavior: ticks keep their cadence while a slow fake compressor runs; compression reads and writes in 1 MiB chunks so peak extra memory does not grow with file size
obligations.source_text: pruning never runs on the tick loop (the thermal controller must keep its poll cadence): it runs on its own thread and compresses by streaming zlib in 1 MiB chunks (wbits 31, gzip format), never gzip.compress of a whole file as ship.py:599 does — a whole cultureos day is 224 MB

obligations.seam: two concurrent prune passes over one tmp records dir
obligations.behavior: interleaved passes end with one complete .gz per day, no raw copy, no exception from a missing raw file, and no removal of the other pass's in-progress .tmp
obligations.source_text: the daemon's pass and 'records prune' can run at the same time safely: the temp file name is unique per process (`YYYYMMDD.jsonl.gz.PID.tmp`), the final rename is atomic, removing the raw file tolerates it already being gone, and a stray .tmp is removed only when it is older than 1 hour (so one pass never deletes the other's in-progress file)

obligations.behavior: expired days are deleted before any compression starts; a compressor raising OSError(ENOSPC) leaves that raw day intact, records the error in the pass result and still processes the other days
obligations.source_text: a pass deletes expired days before it compresses anything, and a failed compress (ENOSPC, I/O error) leaves the raw day in place, is logged, and does not stop the rest of the pass — so a nearly full disk still gets space back

obligations.behavior: a pass that changed something writes one records_pruned row (deleted, compressed, bytes_freed, errors) that iter_records returns, plus one log line; an exception inside the pass is caught and logged and the daemon keeps ticking
obligations.source_text: every pass that changes something writes one 'records_pruned' event row (files deleted, files compressed, bytes freed, errors) to the records and a line to governor.log; a pass that fails never raises into the daemon

obligations.behavior: with a fake clock a year ahead of the newest day file, or with a day file dated after today, nothing is deleted and the pass result carries a clock warning
obligations.source_text: a pass deletes nothing when the wall clock looks wrong: if the newest day file is more than 1 day older than today's UTC date (clock jumped forward), or a day file is dated in the future, the pass logs it and skips deletion

obligations.behavior: a symlink named like a day file pointing outside the records dir is not followed and its target survives; subdirectories are not entered
obligations.source_text: a pass acts only on regular files directly inside <data_dir>/records (and governor.log beside it): it never follows a symlink, never recurses, and never touches a path outside that directory

obligations.behavior: the stride computed for a gzipped day equals the stride for the same raw day, using the gzip ISIZE trailer as the uncompressed size
obligations.source_text: history.py sizes its stride from the uncompressed size of a .gz day (the gzip ISIZE trailer, the last 4 bytes) instead of os.path.getsize, so a 7d request does not parse ~25x more lines than intended and miss its 9-18 s DEADLINE
